editorialNote: Focused KB for Parkinson disease. Therapeutic backbone remains levodopa-carbidopa. The late-stage disease-modifying pipeline has been brutal: prasinezumab (PASADENA phase 2), cinpanemab (SPARK), venglustat, and UCB0599 (minzasolmin) have all failed primary endpoints in recent years. Focused ultrasound, DBS, and continuous subcutaneous apomorphine/foslevodopa infusion (Vyalev, 2024) are the meaningful device/formulation advances. Any PD output that omits Vyalev or fails to flag the prasinezumab/cinpanemab/minzasolmin failures is out of date.

commonComorbidities: REM sleep behavior disorder (often precedes motor PD by years)
Hallucinations and psychosis (often medication-induced or DLB-spectrum)
Impulse control disorder on dopamine agonists
lifestyleCategories: Structured exercise (particularly high-intensity aerobic — Park-in-Shape, SPARX trials)
LSVT BIG and LSVT LOUD therapy
Protein redistribution diet to optimize levodopa absorption
Avoid anti-dopaminergic antiemetics (metoclopramide, prochlorperazine) and typical antipsychotics

items.title: Levodopa and the progression of Parkinson's disease (ELLDOPA)
items.authors: Fahn S, Oakes D, Shoulson I, et al. (Parkinson Study Group)
items.summary: Landmark trial establishing that levodopa does not accelerate PD progression. 361 early-untreated PD patients randomized to placebo, levodopa 150/300/600 mg daily for 40 weeks, then 2-week washout. Dose-dependent symptomatic benefit persisted after washout, arguing against the older 'levodopa toxicity' hypothesis. Foundation for modern early-initiation practice.

keyPassages.quote: The severity of parkinsonism was significantly less in the levodopa groups than in the placebo group by the end of the 40-week treatment period.

items.title: Neurostimulation for Parkinson's disease with early motor complications (EARLYSTIM)
items.authors: Schuepbach WMM, Rau J, Knudsen K, et al.
items.summary: RCT of subthalamic-nucleus DBS added to best medical therapy vs best medical therapy alone in 251 PD patients with early motor complications (mean 7.5 years disease, mean age 52). DBS improved PDQ-39 QoL by 7.8 points, more off-time reduction, fewer dyskinesias. Established that DBS need not wait until end-stage disease.

keyPassages.quote: Mean improvements from baseline to 2 years in the PDQ-39 summary index were 7.8 points in the neurostimulation group and 0.2 points in the medical-therapy group (P=0.002).

items.title: International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society evidence-based medicine review: update on treatments for the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease
items.authors: Fox SH, Katzenschlager R, Lim SY, et al.
items.summary: MDS EBM Committee's foundational PD motor-symptom therapeutics review. Graded every drug class across early PD, motor fluctuations, dyskinesia. Remains the reference for 'efficacious', 'likely efficacious', 'investigational' labels across levodopa, DA agonists, MAO-B inhibitors, COMT inhibitors, amantadine, DBS. Documents impulse-control-disorder risk on dopamine agonists.

items.title: Effect of High-Intensity Treadmill Exercise on Motor Symptoms in Patients With De Novo Parkinson Disease (SPARX)
items.authors: Schenkman M, Moore CG, Kohrt WM, et al.
items.summary: SPARX phase 2 RCT: high-intensity treadmill exercise (~3×/week) in de novo PD was feasible and associated with less motor-score worsening vs usual care over 6 months (NCT01506479).

keyPassages.quote: The mean change in Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale motor score in the high-intensity group was 0.3 compared with 3.2 in the usual care group.

items.title: VYALEV (foscarbidopa/foslevodopa) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: First continuous 24-hour subcutaneous infusion of foscarbidopa/foslevodopa (soluble phosphate prodrugs). FDA-approved October 2024 for advanced PD with motor fluctuations. Significantly reduces 'off' time vs oral IR carbidopa/levodopa. Alternative to intrajejunal levodopa-carbidopa enteral suspension (Duopa/LCIG) without needing PEG-J placement.

keyPassages.quote: VYALEV is indicated for the treatment of motor fluctuations in adults with advanced Parkinson's disease.

items.title: Trial of Prasinezumab in early-stage Parkinson's disease (PASADENA)
items.authors: Pagano G, Taylor KI, Anzures-Cabrera J, et al.
items.summary: Phase 2 RCT of prasinezumab (anti-aggregated α-synuclein antibody, Roche/Prothena) in 316 patients with early untreated PD. Did NOT meet primary endpoint (change in MDS-UPDRS total score at week 52). Some prespecified motor secondary endpoints numerically favored prasinezumab. Roche continued development (phase 2b PADOVA ongoing) despite negative primary — readout late 2024.

keyPassages.quote: Neither dose of prasinezumab led to a significant difference from placebo in the change from baseline in MDS-UPDRS total score at week 52.

items.title: Trial of cinpanemab in early Parkinson's disease (SPARK)
items.authors: Lang AE, Siderowf AD, Macklin EA, et al.
items.summary: Phase 2 RCT of cinpanemab (anti-α-synuclein antibody, Biogen) in 357 patients with early PD. Did NOT meet primary endpoint (MDS-UPDRS parts II + III change at week 52). Biogen halted the cinpanemab PD program.

keyPassages.quote: Cinpanemab did not differ significantly from placebo with respect to changes in clinical measures of PD progression.

canonicalFacts.claim: Levodopa-carbidopa (oral) remains the most effective symptomatic therapy for PD motor symptoms; ELLDOPA refuted the concern that levodopa accelerates disease.
Subthalamic-nucleus DBS benefits PD patients with motor fluctuations well before end-stage disease (EARLYSTIM).
Continuous subcutaneous foscarbidopa/foslevodopa infusion (Vyalev) was FDA-approved October 2024 for advanced PD with motor fluctuations — alternative to Duopa/LCIG.
Anti-α-synuclein monoclonal antibodies prasinezumab (PASADENA) and cinpanemab (SPARK) both failed their phase 2 primary endpoints; cinpanemab program discontinued.

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Structured, progressive aerobic exercise (e.g., SPARX 'moderate-to-high intensity treadmill 3×/week') slows motor decline vs usual care.
Refer for LSVT BIG (motor) and LSVT LOUD (dysarthria) therapy.
Consider protein redistribution diet (limit protein intake to dinner) if motor response fluctuates with meals.
Evaluate and treat constipation aggressively; optimize bowel regimen.
Fall-prevention assessment; physical therapy with balance training.
Treat REM sleep behavior disorder (clonazepam or melatonin) if bed-partner safety at risk.

redFlags: Physicians generally caution against prescribing anti-dopaminergic antiemetics (metoclopramide, prochlorperazine) to PD patients — use ondansetron or trimethobenzamide instead.
Physicians generally caution against prescribing typical antipsychotics (haloperidol, risperidone) for PD psychosis — use pimavanserin, quetiapine, or clozapine.
Physicians generally caution against stopping levodopa abruptly — risk of neuroleptic malignant-like syndrome / parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia.
Literature warns against aducanumab-style anti-amyloid agents for PD — these are approved only for Alzheimer disease.
Stem cell clinics (China, Vietnam, Mexico, India) offering unproven IV MSC infusions for PD — no peer-reviewed efficacy data. FDA warning letters issued to US-linked operators.
Impulse control disorder screening is mandatory on dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole, rotigotine); ask specifically about pathologic gambling, hypersexuality, punding, compulsive shopping.

pipelineDrugs.name: Levodopa/Carbidopa
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved since 1970s; extended-release Rytary 2015; inhaled Inbrija 2018; Crexont (ER bilayer) approved 2024
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Bedrock of PD motor therapy. Crexont is the newest oral ER formulation with longer duration than immediate-release or Rytary.

pipelineDrugs.name: Foscarbidopa / Foslevodopa (Vyalev)
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Soluble phosphate prodrugs delivered as continuous 24-hour subcutaneous infusion
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved October 2024 for advanced PD with motor fluctuations
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Major 2024 approval. Subcutaneous continuous infusion alternative to Duopa/LCIG (which requires PEG-J placement). Patients and clinicians may not yet know this exists.

pipelineDrugs.name: Levodopa-carbidopa intestinal gel (Duopa / LCIG / Duodopa)
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Continuous intrajejunal levodopa-carbidopa infusion via PEG-J pump
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved 2015 for advanced PD with motor fluctuations
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Reference device-assisted therapy for advanced PD. Now competes with Vyalev SC infusion.

pipelineDrugs.name: Apomorphine
pipelineDrugs.status: SC injection approved 2004; sublingual Kynmobi approved 2020
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Rescue therapy for sudden OFF episodes. SC continuous apomorphine infusion approved in EU; US approval also expanded.

pipelineDrugs.name: Rasagiline
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First-line monotherapy option in early PD; adjunct for motor fluctuations.

pipelineDrugs.name: Safinamide
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Adjunct for motor fluctuations; dual mechanism theoretically beneficial for dyskinesias.

pipelineDrugs.name: Opicapone
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Once-daily COMT inhibitor (vs tid entacapone, tolcapone with hepatic warning). First-choice COMT inhibitor for most patients.

pipelineDrugs.name: Amantadine ER (Gocovri, Osmolex)
pipelineDrugs.status: Gocovri FDA-approved 2017 for PD dyskinesia; Osmolex 2018
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Only FDA-approved specifically-for-dyskinesia therapy. IR amantadine is also used off-label.

pipelineDrugs.name: Istradefylline
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Non-dopaminergic adjunct for 'off' time reduction. Novel mechanism.

pipelineDrugs.name: Pimavanserin
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Only FDA-approved therapy specifically for PD psychosis (hallucinations, delusions) without worsening motor symptoms.

pipelineDrugs.name: Prasinezumab
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: IgG1 monoclonal antibody against aggregated α-synuclein
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 2 PASADENA missed primary endpoint 2022; phase 2b PADOVA readout 2024-2025
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Still-active disease-modifying candidate despite missed primary in PASADENA; important to flag accurately as investigational-and-uncertain, not established.

pipelineDrugs.name: Cinpanemab
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Failed. Patients and clinicians still ask — must be addressed as discontinued.

pipelineDrugs.name: Minzasolmin
pipelineDrugs.status: ORCHESTRA phase 2 failed primary endpoint 2024; development halted

pipelineDrugs.name: Gene therapy programs for Parkinson's (early-phase)
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Various AAV gene therapy programs (Voyager VY-AADC, AAV-GDNF, Axovant AXO-Lenti-PD)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Gene therapy programs for PD remain early-phase; no late-stage positive readouts to date.

pipelineDrugs.name: Focused Ultrasound (Exablate)
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA approval: unilateral thalamotomy for essential tremor (2016); unilateral pallidotomy for PD motor symptoms (2021); bilateral pallidothalamic tractotomy under investigation
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Incisionless alternative to DBS for asymmetric tremor-dominant PD or medication-refractory tremor in patients who decline or can't have DBS.

pipelineDrugs.name: Deep Brain Stimulation (STN / GPi)
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved since 1997 (ET) / 2002 (PD); adaptive DBS (aDBS) FDA-approved Feb 2025 (Medtronic Percept RC)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Established for medication-refractory motor fluctuations / dyskinesia. Adaptive/closed-loop DBS is the recent frontier — Medtronic aDBS approved 2025.

excludedAgents.name: Cinpanemab
excludedAgents.reason: SPARK phase 2 failed (NEJM 2022); Biogen halted development. Not a viable therapy.

excludedAgents.name: Minzasolmin (UCB0599)
excludedAgents.reason: ORCHESTRA phase 2 failed primary endpoint 2024; UCB halted development.

excludedAgents.name: Venglustat for GBA-PD
excludedAgents.reason: MOVES-PD phase 2 failed primary endpoint; Sanofi halted the PD indication.

excludedAgents.name: Simvastatin for PD neuroprotection
excludedAgents.reason: PD-STAT negative for motor-progression endpoint. Literature does not support prescribing statin for PD neuroprotection outside cardiovascular-indication range.

excludedAgents.name: Nilotinib for PD
excludedAgents.reason: Multiple phase 2 trials (NILO-PD, others) negative; not recommended for PD.

excludedAgents.name: Unproven stem-cell infusions at offshore clinics (China, Vietnam, Mexico, India)
excludedAgents.reason: No peer-reviewed efficacy data for PD. FDA warning letters to US-linked operators. Patient-safety concern.
